chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 247 — The Gold Box: A Quiet Anchor in Madness
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang hoards a gold box like a lifeline. Bai Lingmiao asks the million-li question. A mother sleeps by his bedside. The quietest chapter cuts the deepest.

lore_anchors.definition: A historical practice where a wealthy noble used a beautiful young woman as a living, reusable piece of toilet paper; represents the extreme class-based dehumanization of feudal Chinese society.
A grotesque parasitic entity from Li Huowang’s alchemical past; he hesitates to consume it, signaling his psychological growth and doubt.
In this chapter, Li Huowang keeps a gold box as a physical anchor; he intends to use it as currency for a supernatural "escape plan" the next time he slips into the other world.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang need so much gold?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is stockpiling it as a physical anchor and a potential escape tool, a “get out of jail free” card for his next involuntary transfer between realities.
A cruel historical practice where nobles employed a beautiful woman as a living, reusable piece of toilet paper, reflecting extreme wealth and dehumanization.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Does Li Huowang want the other world to be real?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He does not know, and that uncertainty is the novel’s core horror; he wants to be sane, but he needs his actions to matter.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang scream for chains at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He feels the shift between worlds starting, and the chains are his way of trying to ground himself or be restrained so he does not harm anyone.
